scope: Proposition 4.6 (The capped-layer hull) of the manuscript “Parabolic intersections in Artin groups” (preprints/Parabolic-intersections-in-Artin-groups-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 254 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4cd7fa316371447c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose x is capped at q on J ∪ ∂J, with J spherical. Let p be the harmonic interpolation of mq(x) on J. Assume mq j(y) ≥ pj (j ∈ J) for every jointly capped y ∈ AJ x. (4.2) Put e = mq(x) − p, which is supported on J. Then eJ belongs to the convex hull of finitely many vectors sJ for which s is supported on J and there are graded subrepresentations SL ⊆ Y q (EL(x)), supp SL ⊆ e J, X L wL dim SL = ϕs. (4.3) If every inequality in (4.2) is strict, eJ is in the ordinary interior of such a hull in RJ . For J = ∅ this uses the convention that {0} is open in R0.
